compound_name: Pomegranate peel extract (mixture; not an isolated compound)
target_or_model: Aβ1-42-infused C57BL/6 mice; AChE activity, amyloid plaque density, BDNF, lipid peroxidation, TNF-α and spatial memory
main_result: Oral pomegranate peel extract (800 mg/kg/day) was associated with reduced AChE activity and amyloid plaque density, increased BDNF expression, reduced lipid peroxidation and TNF-α, and improved performance in the Barnes maze compared with the Aβ model group.
limitations: The intervention was a whole peel extract, so the effect cannot be attributed to one molecule. Animal model only; no demonstration of efficacy in humans.

target_or_model: LPS-induced neuroinflammation in cultured astrocytes and BV-2 microglial cells, and LPS-treated mice; NF-κB, inflammatory markers, APP/BACE1 expression and Aβ1-42
evidence_level: In vitro and in vivo animal experimental study
main_result: Punicalagin reduced LPS-associated inflammatory responses and oxidative-stress markers, inhibited NF-κB activation, and reduced LPS-induced Aβ1-42 generation alongside lower APP and BACE1 expression in the reported models.
limitations: LPS-induced inflammation is not equivalent to Alzheimer’s disease. The study supports experimental anti-inflammatory/anti-amyloidogenic effects, not clinical efficacy or direct enzymatic BACE1 inhibition.

target_or_model: AChE, BChE and BACE1 enzyme assays; APP-overexpressing neuroblastoma cells; Aβ secretion and intracellular ROS
evidence_level: In vitro enzyme and cell-based experimental study
main_result: Among 25 pomegranate-related compounds screened, gallagic acid was reported as a particularly active inhibitor across the studied cholinesterase and BACE1 targets. It reduced Aβ peptide secretion and BACE1/APPsβ expression in the cell model; co-incubation also reduced Aβ42-induced intracellular ROS.
limitations: Preclinical enzyme and cell evidence only. The abstract does not provide all compound-specific numerical IC50 values; consult the full article before reporting quantitative potency. No human efficacy demonstrated.

target_or_model: AChE, BChE and BACE1 enzyme assays; APP-overexpressing neuroblastoma cells; Aβ secretion and BACE1/APPsβ expression
evidence_level: In vitro enzyme and cell-based experimental study
main_result: Castalagin was among the pomegranate constituents investigated against AChE, BChE and BACE1. In the cell model, castalagin reduced Aβ peptide secretion and BACE1/APPsβ expression at the reported treatment concentration.
limitations: Preclinical evidence only. The abstract does not provide all compound-specific enzyme potency values; confirm exact assay results in the full paper. No human efficacy demonstrated.

compound_name: Punicalagin; ellagic acid; pomegranate peel extract; pomegranate aril extract
target_or_model: Aβ1-42-challenged human cell models; pTau-181, ROS, lipid peroxidation, inflammatory cytokines, microglial/macrophage phenotype and neuronal viability
main_result: The study reported that pomegranate polyphenol treatments, including punicalagin, ellagic acid and peel/aril extracts, attenuated Aβ1-42-associated Tau-181 phosphorylation and oxidative/inflammatory effects in the tested cellular models. Ellagic acid showed a strong reduction in pTau-181 in the reported experiments.
limitations: Cell-based evidence only. The study does not establish clinical benefit. Do not claim direct GSK-3β inhibition unless a specific kinase assay supports it.

target_or_model: AChE enzyme; ellagitannin study using Terminalia chebula fruits
evidence_level: In vitro enzyme study; different botanical source
main_result: Punicalagin showed AChE inhibition with a reported IC50 of 0.43 mM in a study of ellagitannins from Terminalia chebula.
limitations: The study material was Terminalia chebula, not Punica granatum. This is not evidence that a pomegranate extract or pomegranate-derived punicalagin preparation was tested in that experiment.

target_or_model: AChE enzyme; ellagitannin study using Terminalia chebula fruits
evidence_level: In vitro enzyme study; different botanical source
main_result: Corilagin inhibited AChE with a reported IC50 of 0.72 mM in a study of ellagitannins from Terminalia chebula.
limitations: The study material was Terminalia chebula, not Punica granatum. Do not present this as a pomegranate-specific experimental result.
